claims.reason: Complete definition over an arbitrary field and a sequence indexed by natural numbers: v(n+2)−2v(n+1)+v(n). No characteristic-zero assumption is present.
Both sequence binders and the field parameter are explicit. The equivalence uses t(n+3), and the third-order recurrence starts at output index 3.
Quantifies over every field, A, B and natural index n. The affine sequence uses the natural-number cast into that field, including in positive characteristic.
Every coefficient sequence t and every pair A, B are quantified. No nonvanishing assumption on t or the affine sequence is included.
The conclusion specifies the affine sequence determined by v(0) and v(1), with equality at every natural index; it is not merely an existential affine representation.
Includes both first-order recurrence hypotheses and a(0)≠0. Later values of a and the multiplier sequence are not assumed nonzero.
Applies to every field-valued sequence and every natural n. Its sum ranges over k<n and is empty at n=0.
The reconstruction uses the initial value, initial first difference and finite sums over k<i<n. It includes n=0 and n=1 without a recurrence hypothesis.
Assumes only that E solves the third-order recurrence. The identity involves products and differences, with no division or nonvanishing requirement.
Under the solution hypothesis for E, the product E·r solves the recurrence exactly when the displayed residual vanishes at every natural index. Zeros of E are permitted.
Includes E(j)≠0 for every natural j. The quotient difference uses truncated natural subtraction, so its index-zero value is zero; IsSolution2 does not use that value.
The supplied withInitial definition resolves the integration convention completely: the result is r0 plus the sum of s(1) through s(j), excluding s(0).
States all three initial identities at indices 0, 1 and 2 for arbitrary r0 and s. There is no condition on s(0).
For every natural j, the increment from j to j+1 equals s(j+1). It does not assert an increment representing s(0).

Retains the solution and everywhere-nonzero hypotheses for E and the reduced-recurrence hypothesis for s. The reconstructed quotient increments agree with s at positive indices, with initial product value E(0)r0.

Defines (2j+ε)(2j+ε−1) using rational casts and rational subtraction. The definition includes j=0 and does not assert nonvanishing there.
Takes the factorial of the natural number 2j+ε and then casts the result to the rationals. Both natural parameters are unrestricted.

Defines a recurrence predicate on rational sequences, with equations at n+3 for every natural n. It adds no integral representation, positivity or initial normalization.

Retains the parity and nonzero-c hypotheses and all three coefficient equalities. The middle transformed coefficient carries the minus sign.
